entry.title: Depth of Maximum of EAS and Mean Mass Composition of Primary CRs from the Spatial and Temporal Distribution of Cherenkov Light According to TAIGA-HiSCORE Data
entry.summary: We present the dependence of the depth of maximum of extensive air showers (EAS), $X_{\max}$, on the energy of the primary particle, as determined from data recorded with the wide-angle Cherenkov array TAIGA-HiSCORE during the 2021--2025 observation seasons. The reconstruction of $X_{\max}$ from the experimental data uses relations obtained from EAS simulations: the dependence on the steepness of the Cherenkov light lateral distribution function ($P$-method) and on the full width at half maximum of the Cherenkov light pulse ($τ$-method). The reconstructed $X_{\max}$ values are converted into the mean logarithmic mass $\langle\ln A\rangle$, which characterizes the primary cosmic-ray mass composition. The results are compared with measurements from Tunka-133 (2017), the Pierre Auger Observatory (2019), LHAASO (2024), TALE (2026), and other experiments.

entry.title: Scattering and bound observables for spinning particles in Kerr spacetime with generic spin orientations
entry.summary: We derive the radial action of a spinning probe particle in Kerr spacetime from the worldline formalism in the first-order form, focusing on linear in spin effects. We then develop a novel covariant Dirac bracket formalism to compute the impulse and the spin kick directly from the radial action, generalizing some conjectural results in the literature and providing ready-to-use expressions for amplitude calculations with generic spin orientations. This allows, for the first time, to find new covariant expressions for scattering observables in the probe limit up to $\mathcal{O}(G^6 s_1 s_2^4)$. Finally, we use the action-angle representation to compute the fundamental frequencies for generic bound orbits, including the intrinsic spin precession, the periastron advance and the precession of the orbital plane.

entry.title: Zeta function in Coulomb background
entry.summary: We calculate the one-loop vacuum energy of a massive scalar field confined to the interior of a sphere with Dirichlet boundary conditions and subject to a Coulomb background potential $α/r$. The spectrum is determined by the zeros of a confluent hypergeometric (Kummer) function, and the corresponding zeta function is constructed and analytically continued to $s=-1/2$. The renormalization is performed by subtracting the divergent part of the zeta function, defined through the heat kernel expansion, which removes the non-decreasing powers of the mass and leaves a finite, physically normalized vacuum energy. While the heat kernel coefficients for the pure Bessel (Coulomb-free) case are well known, the Coulomb contributions to the coefficients are not; we determine them by matching the analytic continuation of the zeta function to the general form of the divergent part, obtaining terms proportional to $α$ and $α^2$. A key technical point is that the uniform asymptotic expansion of the mode generating function cannot be used in full; a part must be retained unexpanded, and an integral representation of the digamma function is used to carry out the analytic continuation. In the infinite-volume limit the renormalized vacuum energy tends to a constant $E_0^{ren,\infty}(α,m)=αe(α/m)$, with a dimensionless function $e$ that depends only on the ratio $\al/m$. This limit shows that a finite, physically meaningful renormalized vacuum energy can be defined for a massive scalar field in the background of a Coulomb source. For $m\to\infty$ it vanishes in accordance with the normalization condition, while for $m\to0$ it diverges, so that the present calculation does not apply to a massless field, pointing to the need of another vacuum state in that case.

entry.title: A Self-Interacting Dark-Matter Route to Supermassive Kerr Black Holes via Super-Eddington Bondi Accretion: Mass-Spin Evolution
entry.summary: Recent JWST observations motivate mechanisms for rapid black-hole growth in the early Universe. Extending our previous Schwarzschild study, we show that critical relativistic Bondi accretion of repulsively self-interacting dark matter remains an efficient super-Eddington channel for Kerr black holes with rotating inflow. Within a stationary equatorial quasi-spherical framework, smooth critical solutions exist over a finite range of inflow angular momentum set by the Kerr marginally bound capture values. Rotation changes the sonic structure and accretion efficiency, while the critical density cancellation and dark-sector/halo matching retain their Schwarzschild form. The resulting rapid growth persists until the finite halo supply becomes limiting. Because the inflow also carries angular momentum, stellar-mass seeds can grow and spin up simultaneously; illustrative population evolutions therefore provide a joint mass--spin route to early supermassive Kerr black holes.

entry.title: Positronium resonance of electric monopoles in quantum spin ice
entry.summary: Quantum spin ice attracts considerable attention due to its remarkable low-energy properties, described by the effective gauge theory, which mimics the quantum electrodynamics (QED). The ``effective" QED in quantum spin ice is beyond the ``real" QED in our universe in many respects. Above all, the effective QED hosts two kinds of gapped particles, the electric monopole, in addition to the magnetic monopole. Among the two monopoles, the electric monopole is of purely quantum origin, and its character has not been well resolved. In this work, we focus on the Rokhsar Kivelson point of the quantum dimer model, as the low-energy description of the quantum XXZ model on a pyrochlore lattice, and address the excitation spectrum of the electric monopoles, by combining the quantum Monte Carlo simulation with the stochastic analytical continuation. Most strikingly, the electric monopole spectrum exhibits clear double-peak structure, corresponding to the bound states and scattering states of electric monopoles. The lower-energy peak is attributed to the exciton-like bound state of an electric monopole pair, a signal of positronium in quantum spin ice. We found that the flippable loop operator serves as a local physical observable to excite a pair of electric monopoles, implying that monopoles can be detected through lattice or optical response.

entry.title: Three-dimensional Bose-Fermi droplets at nonzero temperatures
entry.summary: Using numerical methods, we study the formation of self-bound quantum Bose-Fermi droplets at nonzero temperatures. We describe an attractive atomic Bose-Fermi mixture using quantum hydrodynamics enriched by beyond-mean-field corrections and thermal fluctuations, together with a simplified self-consistent Hartree-Fock model. With these models, we determine that low-temperature droplets with finite lifetimes can exist in free space when the attraction between bosons and fermions is sufficiently strong. Additionally, Bose-Fermi droplets at nonzero temperatures can exist in a box potential in equilibrium with bosonic and fermionic vapor. We discuss the properties of Bose-Fermi droplets at nonzero temperatures in terms of the initial condensate fraction, total atom number, and interspecies attraction strength.

entry.title: Electromagnetic duality degeneracy in dynamical black hole mergers
entry.summary: Electromagnetic duality is a symmetry of the source-free Einstein-Maxwell equations that rotates electric and magnetic fields while leaving the stress-energy tensor invariant. We present the first fully nonlinear realization of this symmetry in dynamical strong-gravity regimes by performing numerical relativity simulations of charged black hole mergers across a continuous duality family. Starting from electrically charged binaries, we generate dyonic and magnetically charged configurations via duality rotations and evolve them within a common numerical framework. We find that all dual configurations exhibit identical spacetime dynamics, while the emitted electromagnetic radiation is related by a rotation of its polarization equal to the duality angle. Our results demonstrate a degeneracy of gravitational observables under electromagnetic duality and provide a concrete mapping between dual configurations at the level of radiation, establishing electromagnetic duality as an organizing principle for dynamical Einstein-Maxwell solutions.

entry.title: Charge-transfer gap size and oxygen hole content as two mechanisms controlling $T_c$ in the Emery model
entry.summary: Investigating the drivers of superconducting critical temperature trends in cuprates is crucial for uncovering the mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity. Here we study this problem in the canonical model of the copper-oxygen plane, the Emery model, with cellular dynamical mean-field theory. Using the Zaanen-Sawatzky-Allen diagram as a guiding framework, we systematically quantify how the maximum superconducting critical temperature $T_c^{\rm max}$ depends on the copper-oxygen energy distance and on the local repulsion on the copper orbital. The latter is the dominant variable in varying $T_c^{\rm max}$. Unexpectedly, $T_c^{\rm max}$ is optimized not only near the charge-transfer insulator to metal boundary, consistent with previous findings, but also deep in the charge-transfer regime, revealing an unexplored mechanism. Then we link model parameters to physical observables, identifying the charge-transfer gap size and the oxygen hole content as two mechanisms controlling $T_c^{\rm max}$. $T_c^{\rm max}$ increases monotonically as the oxygen hole content increases and the charge gap size decreases. Our work provides predictions for proposed realizations of the Emery model with ultracold atoms and a theoretical framework for understanding key experimental trends in hole-doped cuprates.

entry.title: Commuting-check gauging for fault-tolerant logical measurements
entry.summary: Gauging turns a logical operator into a product of local checks, providing a route to logical measurement and lattice surgery. These checks can fail to commute outside the code space, so measuring one can randomize the outcome of another. In this work, we introduce completion qubits that make the checks commute for Clifford $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetries of qubit stabilizer codes. Adding one completion qubit per noncommuting pair preserves the gauged code space and its distance while keeping the checks Clifford. Completion also preserves the low-density parity-check property with a constant-factor qubit overhead. We generalize completion to qudits and establish bounds on the Clifford-hierarchy level of the completed checks in prime dimensions. Global commutation ensures that a fault-free round fixes the syndrome until the next fault and allows us to bound fault propagation independently of the number of measurement rounds. For qubit codes, we show that gauging and ungauging a distance-$d$ parent code implements a logical measurement with circuit fault distance $Ω(d)$ in $O(d)$ rounds. We demonstrate the construction by gauging two toric codes into the $D(D_4)$ quantum double and back, with an explicit circuit whose circuit fault distance equals the parent code distance. Our results provide a framework for fault-tolerant logical measurements using commuting checks, with applications to magic-state preparation by lattice surgery.

entry.title: The low luminosity end of Galactic HMXBs with eROSITA: Establishing a luminosity floor for accreting BeXRBs
entry.summary: We present a first look at the Galactic population of heretofore known HMXBs as observed by SRG/eROSITA during its first four surveys. eROSITA's sensitivity of $\sim10^{-13}\,\mathrm{erg}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$, translating to $10^{32}$-$10^{34},\mathrm{erg}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ in luminosity for most known HMXBs in the Milky Way, has thus far never been reached by any wide-area survey instrument. We present the extended log N-log L distribution of known HMXBs reaching down to $10^{32}\,\mathrm{erg}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ using eROSITA, and show the large scatter that can be induced by source intrinsic variability. We present sub-type resolved luminosity distributions, showing that the Supergiant X-ray binaries (SgXBs) and Be X-ray binaries (BeXRBs) occupy different parts of the overall distribution, and reanalyse RXTE/ASM data and MAXI for comparison to eROSITA. The luminosity regime uncovered by eROSITA allows a systematic study of the "transient" BeXRBs, which are typically below the detection threshold of monitors outside of outburst, and whose low luminosity behavior has been a longstanding question. Signatures of stable accretion at low luminosities have been observed with pointed instruments for a fraction of the overall sample, so far. With the eROSITA results, we posit that accretion outside of outburst is likely the norm, since a vast majority (> 80%) of BeXRBs are detected at luminosities at least an order of magnitude higher than expected for the most X-ray luminous Be stars. We discuss the observed luminosity in the context of cold disk accretion and the "propeller" mechanism. We highlight a small subpopulation of "isolated" Be-stars that reach luminosities comparable to the least luminous BeXRBs, hinting at the presence of compact object companions.

entry.title: Correlation of maximum superconducting critical temperature with copper-oxygen energy distance and oxygen hole content in the Emery model
entry.summary: Identifying microscopic parameters that optimize the maximum superconducting critical temperature $T_c^{\rm max}$ in the canonical model of the copper-oxygen plane of cuprates, the Emery model, remains challenging. Using cellular dynamical mean-field theory at finite temperature, we find that for a fixed charge gap size in the parent charge-transfer insulating state, $T_c^{\rm max}$ unexpectedly increases with increasing the copper-oxygen energy distance, as this favors the transfer of electrons from oxygen to copper orbitals. We show that these findings emerge naturally in the Zaanen-Sawatzky-Allen scheme and capture observed trends in hole-doped cuprates. Overall, our study uncovers that $T_c^{\rm max}$ is optimized in the Emery model under three conditions: upon doping a charge-transfer insulator, close to the charge-transfer insulator to metal boundary, and deep into the charge-transfer regime. While the first two are well-established, uncovering the third is our core contribution. This finding indicates new paths for optimizing $T_c^{\rm max}$.

entry.title: Landau Levels on the Surface of a Cube
entry.summary: We study the quantum mechanics of a charged particle confined to the surface of a cube enclosing a magnetic monopole. The magnetic field is chosen to have a constant magnitude on each face and to point along the outward normal, preserving the rotational symmetry of the cube. We formulate the continuum problem using two gauge patches on the cube surface and show that consistency of the wavefunction gives the Dirac quantization condition. Since an explicit vector potential does not remain invariant under ordinary rotations, we construct gauge-modified rotation operators and use them to classify the eigenstates. Even monopole charges are described by the irreducible representations of the cubic rotation group O, while odd monopole charges require the spinorial representations of the binary octahedral group 2O. We compute the spectrum with a gauge-covariant finite-difference discretization and find Landau-level-like manifolds whose degeneracies are split by the discrete cubic symmetry. We also study the corresponding tight-binding Hofstadter problem on the discretized cube. The resulting spectrum contains the usual magnetic subband structure together with additional gap states localized near the cube corners.

entry.title: Background-independent one-loop renormalization of tensor and scalar primordial spectra
entry.summary: We present a background-independent renormalization framework for one-loop primordial spectra. We apply it to two observables: the scalar-induced tensor spectrum sourced by a minimally coupled spectator field, and the scalar spectrum generated by potential self-interactions. In both cases, the UV part of the loops is isolated and, using the universal WKB behavior of the internal modes, the UV poles are extracted analytically and absorbed into local counterterms without having to specify either the background evolution or the full dynamics of the field running in the loop. This yields finite model-independent expressions for the renormalized spectra amenable to numerical analysis.

entry.title: Measurement of the Neutrino Spectrum along the Galactic Plane with IceCube
entry.summary: We present the first measurement of the variation of the high-energy neutrino flux along the Galactic plane using 10 years of neutrino-induced particle-shower data from the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. In this Letter, we fit both the neutrino flux normalization and the spectral index, in multiple regions along the plane, independent of model expectations. The neutrino flux per solid angle in the inner Galactic region ($\vert l\vert< 30^{\circ}, \vert b\vert < 8^{\circ}$) is approximately five times higher than in the outer Galactic plane ($\vert l\vert>60^{\circ}, \vert b\vert < 8^{\circ}$) at $E_ν=5\mathrm{TeV}$. The spectral indices in the inner and outer region are $γ=2.76^{+0.18}_{-0.15}$ and $γ= 3.13^{+0.57}_{-0.37}$, respectively. Additionally, we compare the same region of Galactic emission measured in $\mathrm{TeV}$ gamma rays by LHAASO ($15^{\circ}<l<125^{\circ}$) to neutrinos, and conclude that the measurements are compatible within uncertainties, under the assumption of hadronic gamma-ray production.

entry.title: Discrete gravitational diagram technique and corrections to the Newtonian potential
entry.summary: To develop a gravitational diagram technique that is ultraviolet finite, we start from Regge's simplicial gravity and use a bell-shaped form of the measure obtained via functional integration over connection. A "hypercubic" structure is considered (some variables are frozen), it is described by the metric $g_{λμ}$ at the sites. The measure is known in closed form if the timelike length scale is fixed at a low level. This is possible in the synchronous gauge (properly softened to remove nonphysical infrared singularities). This gauge also allows, with a refined finite-difference form of the action, to match the analytical properties of the propagator to the continuum case. The metric is parameterized to make the measure Lebesgue. The linear part of this parametrization leads to a discrete form of standard Feynman diagrams that approximates finite continuum diagrams and is finite for infinite ones; the nonlinear part gives new vertices and diagrams. The maximum of the measure is at the edge length scale $b = b_{\rm s} \sim η^{1/2}$, where $η$ defines the free factor like $(- \det \|g_{λμ}\|)^{η/2}$ in the measure and should be a large parameter to ensure true action upon integration over connection. For general perturbative expansion (including both that for the measure and the S matrix) to be free of increasing powers of $η$, its initial point must be at $b$ sufficiently close to $b_{\rm s}$; this appears to be a dynamic mechanism for establishing $b$ as an optimal initial point of the perturbative expansion. This technique is applied to Newton's potential. Some of new diagrams, including potentially large ones, are mutually cancelled. The S matrix expansion is analyzed to consist of standard diagrams. These diagrams form series with a small parameter $η^{-1}$; one-loop diagrams calculated in the literature represent the leading order.

entry.title: Joint probes of dark matter annihilation from neutrino detectors and CMB targets
entry.summary: Dark matter (DM) annihilation into neutrinos provides a promising observational channel targeted by current and forthcoming neutrino detectors. However, the detection of such neutrino fluxes alone cannot uniquely determine their astrophysical or cosmological origin, such as the recent observations from Super-Kamiokande that hint at a small excess of electron antineutrino events. We propose that the effective number of neutrino species and the spectral distortion of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) can serve as complementary observables to probe neutrino signatures from DM annihilation. Using a simple model-independent analysis, we determine the detection windows of these cosmic observables that overlap with the experimental sensitivities from the Super-Kamiokande, Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory, Hyper-Kamiokande, and the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment, showing that joint probes of large DM annihilation to neutrinos with MeV-GeV masses can be achieved by neutrino detectors and CMB experiments.

entry.title: Gravitational Waves from Multiple Cosmic Superstrings and the Overshoot Problem
entry.summary: Post inflationary string cosmology can feature an initial population of multiple species of cosmic superstrings whose tension is controlled by a modulus rolling over a steep potential toward a late-time minimum. We perform a full analysis of the associated dynamical system, finding that overshooting the minimum is prevented by the friction of a radiation background of gravitational waves produced from the early decay of effective strings arising from NS5- and D3-branes wrapped around internal cycles. On the other hand, fundamental strings survive longer and decay when the modulus is oscillating around the minimum and they have about $1/3$ of the total energy density. The spectrum of gravitational waves generated by the decays of these multiple cosmic superstrings, even if diluted by a late epoch of modulus domination, can still result in a high-frequency, multi-peaked signal, offering an observational signature of generic features of string theory.

entry.title: Einstein--Yang--Mills Plane Waves: Uniqueness and an Exact Curvature Double Copy
entry.summary: Coleman found plane waves of Yang--Mills theory that are genuinely non-abelian in four dimensions and yet obey linear field equations, and Güven showed that they remain exact when gravity is included. We study these waves in $D$ dimensions. Coleman's profile, which is linear in the transverse coordinates, is singled out twice: up to gauge, it is the only profile with bounded energy density, and the only one for which the full Riemann tensor equals the color-contracted square of the Yang--Mills field strength that sources it. In anti-de Sitter space, we construct a closed-form family for every $D\geq4$; there, the full Riemann tensor cannot equal this color square. Waves whose transverse space is a sphere are always singular. In quadratic and Gauss--Bonnet gravity, a hyperbolic transverse space avoids this only if the waves defocus light or the higher-curvature terms become comparable to the Einstein term. All solutions extend, with changed coefficients, to generic gravity and gauge theories.

entry.title: Post-Newtonian Global Conservation Laws in the Presence of Sensitive Bodies
entry.summary: The parameterized post-Newtonian (PPN) approach is the state of the art formalism for performing theory independent tests of weak-field gravity, and for constraining possible deviations from Einstein's theory. Within this framework, global conservation laws are useful for the calculation of dynamics and for giving meaning to parameters. In this paper we extend the concept of semi-conservative and fully-conservative theories of gravity to include situations in which compact astrophysical bodies are modeled as masses that are sensitive to their local environment, as relevant for theories that violate the strong equivalence principle. We find that globally conserved quantities can still exist in the presence of such sensitivities, and find their explicit forms when they do. We identify new ways of writing the coefficients that enter into the PPN metric when a theory of gravity admits conserved quantities in the presence of a sensitive body, and demonstrate the applicability of our approach by comparing it to known results in scalar-tensor theories of gravity.

entry.title: Magnetic properties of the Abell 3391-3395 system revealed using wide-field MeerKAT polarimetry
entry.summary: Magnetic fields in cluster outskirts and the intercluster medium are poorly constrained because diffuse synchrotron emission is hard to detect at low surface brightness. Faraday rotation measures (RMs) of polarized background sources can probe foreground large-scale structure. The nearby interacting Abell 3391-3395 system hosts a well-established X-ray bridge, making it an excellent target for studying magnetization in the intercluster environment. We characterize the magnetized environment of Abell 3391/95 and its surroundings by constructing a dense RM grid from wide-field polarimetry. We observed Abell 3391/95 with MeerKAT in full polarization using a three-pointing mosaic. The data were calibrated with direction-independent and direction-dependent techniques and imaged using visibility-plane mosaicing for a large field of view at high sensitivity. Using Faraday synthesis, we formed Faraday cubes and measured RMs for polarized background sources. We defined on- and off-target regions using contours from a wavelet-filtered eROSITA image. We identified 434 polarized sources within the field, with a polarized source density ranging from about 30 sources per square degree in the outer regions to about 110 sources per square degree in the central field, and a field-averaged density of 73 sources per square degree. The clusters show a statistically significant enhancement of RM scatter relative to the off-target region. In contrast, the bridge shows comparatively low RM scatter, while an RM structure-function analysis on matched angular scales yields a tentative indication of larger RM differences in the bridge than off-target. Combined with low per-source depolarization, this suggests a bridge magnetic field relatively ordered on ~10 kpc scales, but less ordered on larger scales. The non-detection of diffuse synchrotron emission in the bridge yields improved upper limits on the emissivity.

entry.title: Scaling at quantum phase transitions above the upper critical dimension
entry.summary: The hyperscaling relation and standard finite-size scaling (FSS) are known to break down above the upper critical dimension due to dangerous irrelevant variables. We establish a coherent formalism for FSS at quantum phase transitions above the upper critical dimension following the recently introduced Q-FSS formalism for thermal phase transitions. Contrary to long-standing belief, the correlation sector is affected by dangerous irrelevant variables. The presented formalism recovers a generalized hyperscaling relation and FSS form. Using this new FSS formalism, we determine the full set of critical exponents for the long-range transverse-field Ising chain in all criticality regimes ranging from the nearest-neighbor to the long-range mean field regime. For the same model, we also explicitly confirm the effect of dangerous irrelevant variables on the characteristic length scale.

entry.title: Kerr-athermal baths enhance cooling in quantum refrigerators
entry.summary: We study a three-qubit quantum refrigerator, with a three-body interaction enabling cooling of the target qubit, coupled to harmonic oscillator baths prepared in stationary Kerr-athermal states. The reservoir occupation probabilities are specified by a Kerr-type preparation Hamiltonian, while the bath dynamics during operation are harmonic. We show that these reservoirs lower the steady-state temperature of the cold qubit relative to the thermal-bath reference. The improvement of steady-state cooling is distinct from that of the minimum transient temperature, which is not universally enhanced. In a parameter regime where the thermal reference exhibits only transient cold-qubit cooling, the engineered Kerr-athermal baths can produce a steady-state temperature below the initial value. We also investigate the dependence of the steady-state temperature and minimum attainable temperatures on the anharmonicity in the bath state. Analysis of bath-currents reveals lower steady-state temperatures with nearly unchanged coefficients of performance, revealing that reservoir engineering leads to cold-qubit cooling.

entry.title: A Common Type II Origin of Galilean and Carroll Superstrings
entry.summary: We show that the relativistic Type-II superalgebras, once the fundamental-string winding charge is retained alongside the momentum, admit a single non-Lorentzian contraction with two invariant translation ideals, whose complementary quotients yield Galilean and magnetic-Carroll superalgebras. The complementary vector charge required for this structure is thus intrinsic to string theory. The IIA realization is particle-like and the IIB realization string-like, a distinction fixed by chirality, and spacelike T-duality relates the two while preserving each non-Lorentzian structure. The same contraction is finite on the doubled Green--Schwarz action, including all fermion terms and local kappa symmetry, where the two supersymmetries appear as the two polarizations of a single worldsheet theory. These results unify two distinct non-Lorentzian corners of string theory within a common Type-II origin and open a route toward a broader web of non-Lorentzian dualities and possible holographic generalizations.

entry.title: The running of Weyl gauged gravity: asymptotic freedom, its obstruction, and a way out
entry.summary: We compute the one-loop beta functions of quadratic gravity in Weyl conformal geometry, the gauge theory of diffeomorphisms and dilatations with a dynamical Weyl gauge boson. The divergences are extracted diagrammatically in the background field method, with a gauge fixing procedure adapted to the semidirect product structure of the gauge group. The Weyl-tensor coupling and the Weyl gauge coupling are asymptotically free, and the running of the latter is special, being independent of the other couplings and of any two-derivative matter content. The obstruction to an ultraviolet completion comes from the square of a Weyl-covariant curvature scalar, denoted $\widehat{R}{}^2$: the flow of the corresponding coupling has no fixed point in the physically interesting region and becomes trivial, the only real fixed points require a decoupled Weyl boson and a tachyonic scalar mode. This also holds when including the Standard Model with any nonminimal Higgs coupling and, more generally, for any matter with two-derivative kinetic terms. Weyl-invariant four-derivative scalars with a sufficiently large coupling to $\widehat{R}{}^2$ can remove the obstruction, producing a fixed point in the physical region that is ultraviolet attractive in all directions and has a nonvanishing Weyl gauge coupling.

entry.title: The Ordinary Days of Extraordinary Blazar 3C 454.3
entry.summary: The blazar 3C 454.3 (z = 0.859) is one of the brightest and most variable flat-spectrum radio quasars in the sky. Here, we present a multi-wavelength analysis of this enigmatic object in its quiescent states during June 2022 and May 2023 coincident with its first X-ray polarimetric and hard X-ray observations with International X-ray Polarimetric Explorer (IXPE) and Nuclear Spectroscopic Telescope Array (NuSTAR). Though no X-ray polarization was detected, NuSTAR detected the source on all occasions during this period. We generated five broadband spectral energy distributions (SEDs)of the blazar using quasi-simultaneous observations taken with the Fermi-Large Area Telescope, NuSTAR, and Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory. The hard X-ray flux measured by NuSTAR exhibited mild flux variations. The SEDs were modeled with a one-zone leptonic emission framework using the JetSet package. The optical-ultraviolet spectrum of 3C 454.3 revealed an upturn which we reproduced with the standard accretion disk model. The X-ray to gamma-ray spectrum of 3C 454 was found to be well explained by the external Compton (EC) process with the seed photons provided by the BLR and accretion disk. These results provide intriguing clues about the multi-wavelength behavior of 3C 454.3 during its quiescent activity state.

entry.title: Investigating the Viability of Dedicated Microhertz Gravitational Wave Pulsar Timing
entry.summary: The microhertz gravitational wave (GW) frequency regime remains one of the least explored regions of the GW spectrum. This is due to the physical limitations of our current and upcoming GW observatories such as LIGO and LISA, which are tuned to dHz and mHz respectively. Proposed experiments targeting the $μ$Hz regime are ambitious, expensive and unlikely to be operational within the next 20 years. Pulsar Timing Arrays (PTAs), with their Galaxy-sized baselines, occupy the other end of the spectrum; the frequencies they are sensitive to are a function of the observing cadence and total dataset timespan. Existing PTA campaigns have cadences and timespans corresponding to the nanohertz regime, however the possibility exists that they can be 'pushed' to detect higher frequencies. This paper investigates the viability of a custom microhertz-sensitive PTA, observing a small number of millisecond pulsars with a daily cadence, over the course of 1 and 2 years respectively. We assume the use of both 100-m and 500-m class radio telescopes for these observations, and an idealised noise model with negligible systematics to determine the most optimistic detection threshold. We compute the sensitivity of our proposed high-cadence PTA configurations to power-law signals and individual GW sources. We find that a 500-m class telescope would likely be able to set new upper limits on individual sources and GW background signals in the $0.1-1~μ$Hz range; while a 100-m class telescope would, in the best case, only match that of the performance of the EPTA second data release in the same range. Finally we consider a possible $μ$Hz PTA consisting of SKA-Mid and DSA observing 24 pulsars; we find this performs on par with the 500-m class while using far less telescope time, presenting a more feasible solution to microhertz-GW pulsar timing.
entry.arxiv:comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics

entry.title: Quantum-geometry-controlled pseudogap and non-Fermi-liquid behavior
entry.summary: The quantum metric plays an essential role in flat-band superconductivity, governing the superfluid weight and coherence length. While previous studies have primarily focused on mean-field superconducting properties, the role of quantum geometry in fluctuation phenomena remains largely unexplored, despite the importance of fluctuations in flat-band systems. To address this issue, we employ a multiorbital T-matrix approximation that retains the orbital structure of the Bloch wave functions. By analyzing models in which the quantum metric can be tuned independently of the band dispersion, we show that an enhanced quantum metric suppresses the fluctuation-induced pseudogap in both flat-band and dispersive-band systems. In dispersive-band systems, this suppression is accompanied by a crossover from non-Fermi-liquid to Fermi-liquid behavior. This spectral evolution suggests a quantum-metric-driven crossover from a BEC-like strong-coupling regime to a BCS-like weak-coupling regime. More broadly, our results establish the quantum metric as a control parameter of interaction-driven fluctuation phenomena beyond mean-field theory.

entry.title: Mitigating oscillatory systematics in MeerKLASS L-band H i intensity maps
entry.summary: HI intensity mapping is a promising probe of the large-scale structure of the Universe, but is limited by foregrounds and instrumental systematics. For the MeerKAT Large Area Synoptic Survey (MeerKLASS) L-band data, it is found that emission line stacking measurement reveals a type of systematics related to the instrument beam. Using simulations with a full-sky electromagnetic beam model, we show that the chromaticity and sidelobes of the MeerKAT beam modulate the frequency-smooth foreground emission and introduce oscillating structures that persist after foreground removal. The beam rotates with respect to the sky between two types of scans, and combining datasets with different beam orientations before foreground cleaning makes the residuals stronger. In MeerKLASS L-band data, processing these two types of scans separately significantly suppresses the oscillating residuals while preserving the stacked HI signal. The ratio of the HI signal amplitude to the systematic fluctuation amplitude increases by 81%. We find an oscillating structure in PCA mode 11 in our previous data processing, but simply removing this mode does not improve the stacked spectrum due to the signal loss. Our strategy can help mitigate spectral ripples that are induced by the beam in future MeerKAT and SKA-Mid surveys.

entry.title: Scaling up spin complexity in ultracold assembled molecules: association and quantum chemistry of Cr-bearing diatomics
entry.summary: The availability of ever more atomic elements in the ultracold regime potentially enables the extension of molecule assembly well beyond bi-alkali systems to targeted chemical species for novel quantum science and technologies. The concurrent need for single-quantum-state control and molecular constants from \emph{ab initio} calculations, especially for previously unexplored species, creates a trade-off between complexity and feasibility. Here, we address this challenge and exploit inter-isotope Feshbach spectroscopy as a tool to study three chromium-bearing diatomics ($^6$Li$^X$Cr, $^{50,52}$Cr$_2$, and $^{53}$Cr$_2$) at different levels of complexity. The extracted molecular properties, including the number of vibrational levels and the dispersion coefficients, allow us to assess quantum chemistry methods. Moreover, our understanding of atomic scattering allows us to assemble LiCr and Cr$_2$ molecules and clarify the observed association pathways with quantum state selectivity. Our results suggest unique prospects for the Li-Cr and Cr-Cr systems, and, more importantly, the experimental viability of a wider class of assembled high-spin molecules for many-body physics and precision measurements.
entry.arxiv:comment: The manuscript has a main text of about 11 pages (7 figures, 5 tables), 4 appendices of 7 pages (5 figures, 4 tables) and 95 references

entry.title: SuperWIMPs in the Kination Era: Imprints on $N_{\rm eff}$ and CMB Spectral Distortions
entry.summary: We investigate how the late-time decays of unstable particles into dark matter and neutrinos can leave measurable imprints on both cosmological observables and collider experiments. We study this mechanism within the scotogenic model, where the lightest singlet fermion $N_1$ serves as the dark matter candidate and is produced via the late decay of the lightest inert doublet scalar via the superWIMP mechanism. By incorporating a kination-dominated era in the early Universe, the altered expansion rate allows to match the observed $N_1$ relic density in parameter regions that would be underabundant in standard cosmology. The energy exchange between the injected neutrinos and photons resulting from the late-time decay can produce CMB spectral $μ$-distortions, detectable shifts in the effective number of relativistic species $N_{\rm eff}$, or both simultaneously. Concentrating on the lightest component of inert doublet scalars with masses between $200$ and $500~\text{GeV}$, we find that these cosmological signals are accompanied by complementary signatures accessible at the LHC. Although our analysis is derived within the scotogenic framework, our findings apply more broadly to scenarios in which the unstable particle undergoes late-time out-of-equilibrium decay to produce dark matter and non-thermal neutrinos, offering how future CMB measurements and collider searches can jointly probe dark matter production and the early Universe's thermal history.

entry.title: Collective excitations in quantum gravity condensates
entry.summary: A central open problem in quantum gravity is to understand how continuum spacetime emerges from quantum-geometric degrees of freedom in a background-independent setting. A many-body perspective suggests that spacetime emerges as a hydrodynamic phase of many atoms of quantum geometry. This idea underlies several approaches to quantum gravity, and it has been explicitly realised in the group field theory formalism. However, quantum fluctuations beyond the mean-field regime remain largely unexplored. We fill this gap by importing Bogolyubov theory to quantum gravity condensates, showing that leading beyond-mean-field effects manifest as collective excitations, in direct analogy with phonons in laboratory Bose-Einstein condensates. We implement the construction in a tractable group field theory model, where condensates of quantum-geometric atoms reproduce nonsingular expanding cosmologies, and derive the leading beyond-mean-field corrections to the emergent Friedmann dynamics. These results identify a new class of quantum-gravity excitations and establish a controlled bridge between microscopic quantum-gravitational dynamics, many-body collective phenomena, and signatures of spacetime emergence.

entry.title: Rotating the Replica: Twisted Rényi Coefficients from CFT Operator Counting
entry.summary: We show that twisting vacuum Rényi entropies by a spatial rotation reveals conformal field theory data governing the asymptotic counting of spinning operators. For a ball in four dimensions, the logarithmic coefficients of these angular-momentum-twisted Rényi entropies are determined by rotating-sphere thermal data to all orders in the local derivative expansion, including the Weyl-anomaly contribution. We test this relation in free theories and in strongly coupled, large-$N$ $\mathcal N=4$ Yang--Mills theory using holography.
entry.arxiv:comment: 5 pages of main text, with appendices and Supplemental Material

entry.title: Topology Obstructs Pure Foundation Neural Quantum States
entry.summary: Foundation models for ground states in spin-1/2 systems are a promising method for problems ranging from quantum chemistry to identifying new phase diagrams. Nearly all such models are currently pure-states that condition on the Hamiltonian's parameters, whose Monte Carlo samples give energy estimates according to the variational principle. In this contribution, we show that this representation is topologically obstructed. For any gapped Hamiltonian family whose ground-state bundle is non-trivial, every continuous normalized state-vector model has zero fidelity with the ground state at some parameter value in the Hamiltonian family. For that value, the energy is at least one spectral gap, $Δ$, with an $O(Δ)$ gap in an open-neighbourhood of that point. We show that this is a sufficient no-go also in the case of degenerate ground-state manifolds, time dynamics, and periodic systems with mixed space-time topology, demonstrating these obstructions on one- and two-qubit systems. We discuss how this causes a spike in the fidelity susceptibility, giving a numerical signature of a phase-transition where there is none. Finally, we show that operator-valued models canonically avoid these obstructions and preserve topological information, implying a structural necessity in representation for foundation neural quantum states.

entry.title: How much dark matter really matters?
entry.summary: Strong gravitational lensing is a key probe to trace dark matter. It assumes that mass curves spacetime so that light from a background source is deflected on its way to the observer. If dark matter contributes the major part to a massive cosmic structure, reconstructing the latter from strong-lensing observables allows us to infer characteristics of dark matter. Standard reconstructions fit a pre-defined mass-density model to the data. In this essay, I show how these mass models over-estimate the dark-matter contents of light-deflecting masses. Eliminating these models from the reconstruction reveals that observations directly constrain local properties of light-deflecting masses. How much dark matter is really needed in strong-gravitational-lensing effects and how much do we make up by our model choices?
entry.arxiv:comment: Honorable mention in the Gravity Research Foundation Essay Contest (published in IJMP D)

entry.title: Universal Fold Caustics in Anharmonic Matter-wave Lenses
entry.summary: Caustics provide a universal connection between classical ray focusing and structured wave patterns. We theoretically investigate this connection in non-linear matter waves focused by a short-duration anharmonic lens acting on a Bose-Einstein condensate. A semi-classical description shows how the leading cubic aberration transforms the harmonic focal point into a fold caustic, whose local wave field is described by an Airy canonical integral. Three-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii simulations show that mean-field interactions modify the near-focus density and longitudinal momentum distribution, producing a secondary momentum-space feature absent from the non-interacting evolution. We quantify the information about the effective interaction strength carried by the $1D$ distribution using classical Fisher information and maximum-likelihood estimation. We obtain a relative uncertainty of $2.7\times10^{-3}$ for a sample of $10^5$ detected points along $z$. These results establish a framework for studying interaction-driven departures from single-particle caustic universality and promote matter-wave lenses as a sensitive probe of mean-field interactions.

entry.title: CMB Bounds on Primordial Black Holes via Radiation Capture: Linear Perturbations
entry.summary: We investigate the gravitational interaction between primordial radiation, consisting of photons and ultra-relativistic neutrinos, and primordial black holes (PBHs), and study its imprint on the anisotropies of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). Assuming that PBHs are immersed in the cosmic radiation background, we introduce a covariant energy-momentum transfer four-vector to describe the gravitational capture of radiation by PBHs. We extend the background-level framework of M. Farhang and S. M. S. Movahed [Phys. Rev. D 114, 083533 (2026)] to an inhomogeneous Universe at linear order by consistently modifying the perturbed continuity and Euler equations to account for both energy and momentum transfer. We use the imprint of this interaction on the CMB to place novel constraints on the PBH abundance, $f_{\rm pbh}$. We show that these constraints are up to two orders of magnitude tighter than those obtained from background-only analyses and exhibit a strong dependence on the PBH mass. Using Planck temperature and polarization data, we constrain the PBH fraction to $f_{\rm pbh} \lesssim 0.05-0.002$ for $M$ in the range $10^{15}-10^{17} M_\odot$. Furthermore, sensitivity forecasts for a cosmic-variance-limited survey with $\ell_{\rm max}=7000$, assuming a fiducial $f_{\rm pbh}=0$, yield projected bounds of $f_{\rm pbh} \lesssim 10^{-2}-2\times 10^{-4}$ over the mass range $10^{13}-10^{17} M_\odot$.

entry.title: Exclusive Quark and Gluon Dijet Production as Probes of GPDs at Collider Energies
entry.summary: We study exclusive electroproduction of dijets in the collinear factorization framework as a probe of generalized parton distributions (GPDs). For quark dijet production, we extend previous analyses by including contributions from helicity GPDs and by assessing an additional leading-order electromagnetic channel governed by elastic nucleon form factors. Furthermore, we investigate exclusive gluon dijet production. We compare our prediction to HERA data and provide projections for measurements at the future Electron-Ion Collider.

entry.title: Exploring the near-kernel sector of quantum reduced loop gravity
entry.summary: We study the near-kernel sector of the Hamiltonian constraint operator in the one-vertex model of quantum reduced loop gravity using exact diagonalisation methods and variational Monte Carlo methods with neural quantum states. The analysis is based on the symmetric Hamiltonian containing both Euclidean and Lorentzian contributions, and on the variational minimization of the positive quadratic operator $\hat{Q}=\hat{C}^2$, where $\hat{C}$ is the symmetric Hamilton constraint, in truncated Hilbert spaces with spin cutoff up to $j_\text{max}=1001$. In the cases where exact diagonalization is possible, the eigenspace of lowest eigenvalue is one- or two-dimensional, and the eigenvalue, as well as the structure of the eigenstates depends on the cutoff. These ground states are entangled across the three edges. The variational method does not find the lowest eigenspace, but near kernel states, i.e., states with components in a number of low lying eigenspaces. For low cutoffs, they also do not factorize across the three edge degrees of freedom. At larger cutoffs, it increasingly finds near kernel states that factorize over the edges, matched with near-unit fidelity by reduced Thiemann coherent states. We discuss some indication that these states are the optimal near-kernel states if factorization is assumed.

entry.title: Two-Loop $n$-Point Identical Helicity Amplitude for Gravity Minimally Coupled to a Chiral Fermion
entry.summary: Motivated by recent developments in the two-loop identical-helicity sector of gauge theory when the one-loop self-dual integrability anomaly of Bardeen and Cangemi, or the equivalent twistor-space version of Costello and Paquette, vanishes, we compute the two-loop four-point identical-helicity amplitude in gravity coupled to a single chiral fermion, for which the corresponding self-dual anomaly also vanishes. We show that the infrared-subtracted amplitude is purely rational and proportional to the identical-helicity tree amplitude of pure gravity with a single insertion of the operator $R^3$. Using this connection, we obtain a closed-form expression for the two-loop $n$-point identical-helicity amplitude in gravity minimally coupled to a fermion. We do so by first obtaining the corresponding identical-helicity gauge-theory tree amplitude with a single $F^3$ insertion using a chiral bootstrap. We then convert these $n$-point gauge theory amplitudes using Kawai-Lewellen-Tye to obtain gravity amplitudes with an $R^3$ insertion, which are necessarily equal to the desired two-loop identical helicity amplitudes of gravity coupled to a chiral fermion. As a nontrivial check, we explicitly verify crossing symmetry and the expected soft limits of our expressions through 13 points.

entry.title: Next-to-next-to-leading gravitational radiation-reaction corrections to quasi-elliptic and quasi-hyperbolic compact binary orbits
entry.summary: We apply the Lagrange method of variation of constants to compute the radiation-reaction (RR) corrections to the quasi-elliptic and quasi-hyperbolic motion of compact binary systems at 4.5PN order, i.e., at next-to-next-to-leading order in the RR. We rely on the recent determination of the 4.5PN RR acceleration, in a general frame and in the center-of-mass frame, in harmonic coordinates. The non-local effects, due to the tails at 4PN order and to the gravitational-wave recoil at 4.5PN order, are carefully evaluated. Although the calculation is implemented differently in the quasi-elliptic and quasi-hyperbolic cases (different perturbation equations and choices of orbital parameters), we verify by analytic continuation that the results for the local effects are equivalent in the two cases.

entry.title: Too shy to spin? Cosmic wallflowers as proto-globular clusters
entry.summary: We investigate the rotational properties of star-forming clusters at $z \sim 7.6$ in the high-resolution simulation MassiveBlackPS, focusing on two formation channels: clusters forming in galactic discs via gravitational instability and isolated circumgalactic systems, referred to as cosmic wallflowers, born out of cosmic filaments. Using stellar kinematics, we compare their rotational velocities, $v_{\rm rot}$, and rotational support, $v/σ$, to study whether formation environment leaves a clear dynamical imprint. We find a clear separation, wherein cosmic wallflowers systematically have lower rotational velocities and span a wide range in $v/σ$, whereas the identified disc clusters are strongly rotation-dominated and extend to higher $v_{\rm rot}$. When combined with stellar surface densities, a subset of the low-$v_{\rm rot}$ cosmic wallflowers lie surprisingly close to the observed globular cluster population in the Milky Way, whereas disc clusters remain offset. Within the cosmic wallflower population, we identify two regimes: lower-density, weakly rotating systems that overlap with these globular cluster properties, and denser, more rotationally supported systems that likely follow a different evolutionary pathway, possibly linking them to the origin of massive black hole seeds at high redshift. We further find that the gas content correlates with this behaviour, with gas-rich cosmic wallflowers preferentially occupying this low-rotation regime. This all suggests that environment and baryonic content together play a key role in setting the initial dynamical state and possible fate of clusters. In particular, weakly rotating, gas-rich cosmic wallflowers emerge as natural proto-globular cluster candidates, potentially evolving towards present-day systems through angular momentum loss and dynamical heating.

entry.title: Connate Topological Superconductivity and Vortex-Position-Controlled Majorana Modes in the Intergrowth Superconductor Th$_2$Mo$_2$Ir$_2$Si$_4$C
entry.summary: The recently synthesized intergrowth compound Th$_2$Mo$_2$Ir$_2$Si$_4$C is an experimentally established bulk superconductor whose topological electronic structure remains unexplored. Here, we identify it as a candidate for connate topological superconductivity and reveal two microscopic routes to vortex Majorana zero modes. First-principles and tight-binding-model calculations uncover Mo--Th band inversion and helical surface states enabled by interorbital spin--orbit coupling between Mo--d$_{xz/yz}$ and Th--d$_{x^2-y^2}$ orbitals. Vortex Bogoliubov--de Gennes calculations further establish a relatively robust surface-state-associated Kitaev phase and a weakly gapped, Th-orbital-derived Kitaev phase. For the latter, shifting the vortex core closes and reopens the vortex-line gap and reverses its one-dimensional topological invariant, consistent with an effective Kitaev-chain mass inversion. Finite-length-vortex calculations reveal distinct spatial and spin-resolved signatures of their Majorana end modes. The orbital Kitaev phase can also exist without helical surface states in a modified model. Although the small orbital-derived gap limits quantitative predictions of experimental observability in this compound, the uncovered mechanism suggests a route to Majorana vortices in multiorbital superconductors beyond the conventional surface-state scenario.
entry.arxiv:comment: 7 pages, 4 figures; Supplemental Material included (19 pages, 14 figures)

entry.title: On a cosmological Oppenheimer-Snyder model: matching McVittie and FLRW spacetimes
entry.summary: We consider the necessary and sufficient conditions for the smooth matching of an expanding McVittie spacetime and a spatially flat FLRW spacetime across a general hypersurface: a hypersurface of arbitrary causal character, where the character possibly changes from point to point. We identify and completely characterize a number of special cases. In the general case, we show that the full set of matching conditions is equivalent to a 3-dimensional non-linear system of first order ODEs, subject to a single initial value constraint. Taking the perspective that the McVittie region is specified, we prove a semi-global existence result for this system and interpret these solutions in terms of the physical set-up. Solutions exist and are unique globally to the future. In this direction, the required FLRW spacetime exists and is unique and the matching hypersurface exists almost everywhere and is unique. However, the necessary embedding conditions for the hypersurface necessarily fail at least once - but only at isolated points - along the putative hypersurface. To the past, the matching hypersurface extends to meet the past singularity of the McVittie region. We determine the causal character of the matching hypersurface in these limits, and consider the implications for the existence (or otherwise) of an isotropic source of the McVittie cosmological black hole spacetime. We find that generically, the matching hypersurface has spacelike as well as timelike portions, and so the isotropic region cannot be considered to be an interior for the McVittie exterior. This is in distinction to the Oppenheimer-Snyder model, in which an isotropic dust sphere matches across an everywhere-timelike boundary to the Schwarzschild exterior. On the basis of the sometimes-spacelike nature of the hypersurface, we conclude that an isotropic source of the McVittie spacetime does not exist in a global sense.
entry.arxiv:journal_ref: Classical and Quantum Gravity, Volume 43, Number 21, (2026)

entry.title: Three-charge black holes from the worldsheet
entry.summary: We consider the general asymptotically flat, doubly-rotating, three-charge black hole uplifted to a family of NS5-F1-P black brane solutions of Type IIB supergravity. We construct a null-gauged WZW model whose target-space geometry reproduces this background in the NS5 decoupling limit, and show that the gauging parameters precisely satisfy the appropriate consistency conditions on the perturbative string spectrum. Through an analytic continuation and an appropriate limit, this model relates to a recently studied construction describing strings on smooth, horizonless geometries. We further analyze the supersymmetric and extremal three-charge configuration, corresponding to the ten-dimensional uplift of the (NS5-decoupled) BMPV black hole, and show that it requires a novel class of null-gauged WZW models. Our construction provides explicit examples of worldsheet CFTs that capture string dynamics on certain black hole geometries with linear dilaton asymptotics.

entry.title: Inaccessibility of the Schwarzschild Singularity to Quantum Probes
entry.summary: We revisit the Schwarzschild singularity in a semiclassical setting where the background geometry is classical and quantum effects enter through Bohmian (quantal) trajectories associated with a Klein-Gordon wave function. Using the Madelung-Bohm decomposition of the Klein-Gordon wavefunction, we show that the quantum-modified motion is equivalent to geodesic motion in an effective metric conformally related to Schwarzschild, with a conformal factor fixed by the wavefunction amplitude. Solving the wavefunction equation near $r\to 0$ determines this factor and yields finite curvature invariants, in suitable coordinates the interior extends smoothly and the effective spacetime is geodesically complete. Our result suggests that quantum probes on a prescribed classical background can experience an operationally regular effective geometry, even though the underlying Schwarzschild spacetime itself remains classically singular.

entry.title: Matrix-vector models for the 3D Ising CFT
entry.summary: The construction of three-dimensional conformal field theories (3D CFTs) using interacting fermions in the lowest Landau level on a sphere has recently proven remarkably efficient, while it differs from that of conventional field theories on the fuzzy sphere. Focusing on the 3D Ising CFT, we consider a class of models that are defined by deformed Hamiltonians specified by a function which controls how the interaction is damped at high angular momenta, and this class includes the original model. We show that each model in the class can be reformulated in a basis-independent manner as a matrix--vector quantum-mechanical model, and, upon integrating out the fermionic vectors, as a matrix model. We then focus on a Gaussian choice, for which the bosonic matrices acquire a heat-kernel propagator whose width is controlled by a parameter $ξ$. Through exact diagonalization with the number of fermions up to $16$, we find that the low-energy spectra of the deformed Hamiltonians at criticality agree with those in the 3D Ising CFT for a range of $ξ$. We thus obtain matrix-model realizations of the 3D Ising CFT that, in contrast to conventional fuzzy-sphere field theories, show no sign of UV/IR mixing in the low-lying spectrum.

entry.title: Deviations from Kerr: Critical curves and photon-ring critical parameters for general observer inclinations
entry.summary: We study critical curves and photon-ring critical parameters in stationary, axisymmetric spacetimes with separable null geodesics and Kerr angular structure. A Kerr-relative decomposition of the radial metric functions gives analytic first-order departures of these observables for observers at general inclination. The critical curve's signed normal displacement factorizes as $\tilde u_n=\tilde F_{\mathrm K}\mathscr C$, where $\tilde F_{\mathrm K}$ depends only on the Kerr reference geometry and $\mathscr C$ is an explicit combination of optical metric deviations. The demagnification exponent, time delay, and azimuthal advance are evaluated at a common position angle on the observer screen. Intrinsic relations among the exact observables express the optical information shared by the curve, time delay, and azimuthal advance, while demagnification additionally depends on radial instability. Applications to representative metrics illustrate how different radial deformations produce distinct departures from Kerr around the critical curve. Comparisons with exact finite-deformation profiles and independent numerical calculations verify the first-order predictions on regular, accessible exterior photon-shell branches.

entry.title: New interpretation of the Minkowski limit of $R^2$ gravity
entry.summary: It is well-established that the Minkowski limit of pure $f(R)=R^2$ gravity breaks down, unlike that of full Starobinsky theory $f(R)=R+αR^2$. We provide a novel interpretation of this phenomenon using the recent thermal analogy between scalar-tensor gravity and Eckart's relativistic dissipative fluids. In this framework, we show that approaching the Minkowski background corresponds to a diverging effective ``gravitational temperature'' along certain non-stationary FLRW trajectories, while the gravitational temperature remains identically zero along the exact de Sitter family. This perspective naturally rephrases the strong coupling problem as a thermal singularity, demonstrating that $R^2$ gravity departs infinitely far from General Relativity rather than recovering it.

entry.title: Hall Viscosity in the Quark-Gluon Plasma
entry.summary: We study the Hall viscosity of the quark gluon plasma (QGP) created in non-central heavy-ion collisions. In the presence of a strong magnetic field or vorticity, rotational symmetry is broken from $O(3)$ to $O(2)$, allowing for two independent Hall viscosities associated with shear deformations transverse and parallel to the symmetry-breaking direction. We find the corresponding constitutive relations by extending the kinetic-theory mechanism to three spatial dimensions and provide parametric estimates of the Hall viscosities under realistic QGP conditions. Both kinetic-theory and holographic estimates indicate that Hall viscosities are comparable in magnitude to the shear viscosity at zero magnetic field. We further show that Hall viscous stresses at hydrodynamic initialization can be as large as standard viscous corrections and identify observable consequences in flow and event-plane correlations.

entry.title: Magnetotropic signatures of Fulde-Ferrell Pairing in a Pauli-limited superconductor
entry.summary: Resonant torsion magnetometry measures the angular curvature of the free energy and is sensitive to magnetic anisotropy. We calculate its response for a clean Pauli-limited superconductor with single-plane-wave Fulde-Ferrell pairing. Field rotation drives a first-order transition from the uniform condensate into the finite-momentum phase and a continuous transition into the normal state. The first-order line produces a sharp softening whose integrated weight is fixed by the magnetization jump, so the dip alone does not identify finite momentum. The distinguishing response is a broad softening inside the Fulde-Ferrell phase, caused by relaxation of the gap and pairing momentum, followed by a finite step at the upper critical field.

entry.title: Rapid Graviton Thermalization through a Scalar--Gauss--Bonnet Coupling
entry.summary: We show that gravitons can thermalize much faster than the universe expands in an effective scalar-mediated model. A thermal fermion bath maintains a massive scalar close to equilibrium, while scalar decay and inverse decay, $φ\rightleftarrows g+g$, drive the graviton distribution toward a Bose--Einstein distribution with zero chemical potential. We establish this equilibrium state and calculate how it is reached from an initially empty graviton sector. For a scalar mass of $1\,{\rm TeV}$, an interaction scale $Λ_{\rm int}=m_φ/0.03$, and a Yukawa coupling $y=0.03$, the graviton occupations approach their equilibrium values to within $0.1\%$ over $0.1\leq p/T\leq5$ after approximately $0.024$ initial Hubble times, including cosmic expansion and energy transfer from the bath. This interval contains the thermal energy-spectrum peak. The scalar remains close to equilibrium, its vacuum decay widths are narrow, and the graviton interaction is perturbative over the reaction domain. Assuming the effective theory applies on this domain, our results demonstrate that gravitons can reach near-thermal equilibrium under these conditions. We also derive the present-day thermal spectrum for a specified decoupling and entropy history.

entry.title: Such stuff as magic is made on: compact operator algebra, stabilizer polytope and the structure of reduced density matrices in a Kitaev spin liquid
entry.summary: Quantum many-body systems exhibit rich and complex behaviour. Magic has recently emerged as a powerful new diagnostic for probing such systems, complementing other key features such as many-body entanglement. Here, starting from an investigation of the onset of magic within subsystems of a larger many-body quantum system, we show that intricate structures emerge which shed important light on the underlying many-body physics. Focusing on the Kitaev honeycomb model, we first identify the temperature below which local subsystems acquire magic. Remarkably, we find that the optimal magic witnesses active at the onset of magic reveal compact operator spaces that continue to capture the local thermal states throughout their subsequent evolution. For the six-site hexagonal marginal, this connection can be made stronger: the same operator space emerges independently from the symmetries of the local marginal and forms the symmetry-resolved plaquette algebra. When these symmetries are realized exactly, the local state lies entirely within this algebra and the reduced robustness of magic is equal to the full robustness of magic. The same reduced description can also be applied to other local quantum resources, which we illustrate using genuine multipartite entanglement. Furthermore, the operator spaces possess a rich algebraic structure in the form of finite-dimensional Euclidean Jordan algebras, with a natural interpretation in terms of bond and bond-cycle operators. Our general methodology therefore show how the onset of local magic can reveal a compact, physically meaningful operator structure underlying the finite-temperature Kitaev spin liquid, and opens up a new avenue towards reduced descriptions of quantum resources in many-body systems.

entry.title: Quantum Gravity from Fractal Entanglement Geometry
entry.summary: In this work, we explore the possibility that spacetime geometry may emerge from the entanglement structure of an underlying quantum-information network. We develop an exploratory framework, termed Fractal Entanglement Quantum Gravity (FEQG), in which information-theoretic correlations provide a candidate pregeometric structure from which aspects of geometry, quantum dynamics, and gravity may arise. An information-based distance on the correlation graph is considered as a possible means of relating quantum correlations to geometric separation. The framework also investigates whether scale-dependent and fractal properties of the underlying structure could lead to dimensional flow, potentially approaching an effective dimension of two near the Planck scale. Within a scale-relativistic perspective, nondifferentiable trajectories and stochastic descriptions are examined as possible ingredients in an effective quantum dynamics; however, the emergence of the Schrödinger equation from the network structure remains to be established. Similarly, the relation between evolving correlations and gravitational dynamics is explored through candidate generalized field equations, while recovering Einstein gravity in an appropriate macroscopic limit remains an open problem. Potential phenomenological consequences include dimensional reduction, modifications to gravitational potentials, and possible deviations from standard quantum mechanics at ultrashort scales. These possibilities are not presented as established predictions, but as directions for further investigation. FEQG thus provides a research program for examining whether quantum-information structure, fractal geometry, and gravitational phenomena can be connected within a common framework.

entry.title: Measuring the Hubble Constant Using Strongly Lensed Gravitational Wave Signals
entry.summary: The measurement of the Hubble constant $H_0$ plays an important role in the study of cosmology. In this letter, we propose a new method to constrain the Hubble constant using the strongly lensed gravitational wave (GW) signals. By reparameterizing the waveform, we find that the lensed waveform is sensitive to the $H_0$. Assuming the scenario that no electromagnetic counterpart of the GW source can be identified, our method can still give meaningful constraints on the $H_0$ with the information of the lens redshift. We then apply Fisher information matrix and Markov Chain Monte Carlo to evaluate the potential of this method. For the space-based GW detector, TianQin, the $H_0$ can be constrained within a relative error of $\sim$ 0.3-2\%, using a single strongly lensed GW event. Precision varies according to different levels of electromagnetic information.

entry.title: A new product formula for $(z;q)_\infty$, with applications to asymptotics
entry.summary: We express the $q$-Pochhammer symbol $(z;q)_\infty$ as an infinite product of gamma functions, analogously to how Narukawa expressed the elliptic gamma function as an infinite product of hyperbolic gamma functions. This identity is used to obtain asymptotic expansions when $q$ tends to $1$.

entry.title: Semiclassical Asymptotics of Entanglement in Torus-Link States
entry.summary: We investigate the entanglement entropy of topological quantum states associated with $T_{d,\,dn}$ torus links in (2+1)-dimensional SU(2) Chern--Simons theory at level $k$. These links consist of $d$ components with pairwise linking number $n$, and the corresponding link-complement states provide a natural setting to study multipartite entanglement in topological quantum field theories. We analyze the semiclassical limit $k\to\infty$ of the entanglement entropy by deriving the asymptotic behavior of the moments of the reduced density matrix. To achieve this, we decompose the integrable-representation space into left-edge, right-edge, and bulk regions and employ the stationary-phase method to evaluate their respective contributions. We find that the leading asymptotic behavior is governed entirely by the two edge regions, while the bulk contribution is asymptotically suppressed. The resulting expression for the limiting entanglement entropy is given in terms of Hurwitz zeta functions and exhibits a dependence on the residue class of $k$ modulo $n$. We further investigate the dependence of the limiting entanglement entropy on the winding parameter $n$ and the number of link components $d$. In the large-$d$ limit, the entropy reduces to a binary entropy determined by two normalized weights associated with the left and right edges. Finally, we show that the two iterated limits, $k\to\infty$ and $d\to\infty$, commute, reproducing the result obtained previously by taking the large-party limit first.

entry.title: Cosmological Collider Signals From a Triangle Loop
entry.summary: Triangular loop signals appear frequently in cosmological collider models but their analytical forms remain unknown due to multiple technical challenges. Here, we determine for the first time the leading analytical cosmological collider signals generated by a massive scalar triangle loop in inflationary bispectrum and trispectrum. Combining a directional cutting rule with partial Mellin-Barnes representations, we obtain both the local and nonlocal trispectrum signals in a soft limit and derive the leading signal in the squeezed bispectrum. Remarkably, all these signals are reproduced by the corresponding bubble diagram with a single effective pinched coupling. Signals beyond leading order and cases with arbitrary internal masses, spins, and interactions can be generated within the same framework. Our approach also provides a systematic route to extracting analytical loop signals from general cosmological correlators.

entry.title: Measurements of $C\!P$ violation with charm hadrons at Belle and Belle II
entry.summary: Recent searches for $C\!P$ violation in charm-hadron decays at Belle and Belle II are presented. The measurements cover $D^+_{(s)}\toηh^+$, $D\toππ$, $D^0\to K_S^0K_S^0$, and $D^0\toπ^+π^-π^0$, together with the singly Cabibbo-suppressed baryon decays $Ξ_c^+\toΣ^+h^+h^-$ and $Λ_c^+\to ph^+h^-$, where $h=π,K$. The Belle II analyses use the Run~1 data sample of $428\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$, supplemented by $980\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ of Belle data for the $K_S^0K_S^0$ measurements. We report preliminary results for the $ηh^+$ modes, complementary tests of the isospin structure of $D\toππ$, and an application of inclusive charm-flavor tagging. The first individual decay-rate asymmetries in these three-body charmed-baryon modes also provide tests of $U$-spin symmetry. All reported asymmetries are consistent with $C\!P$ symmetry within the present precision.
